title: Mia runs a chemistry lesson
topic: A teacher named Mia gives a chemistry lesson; a clear liquid turns red in a beaker, a boy asks about the colour, steam rises from a flask, the students note the result, the lesson ends with the bell
tail_E: On the way out every student takes off the goggles and the white lab
target_note: 'coat' is the near-obligatory completion of 'the white lab' in a chemistry-lesson context (goggles, beaker, burner, flask); the word occurs nowhere in the units or the tail, and neither does its German equivalent (Kittel / Mantel). ' coat' is a single Pythia token (id 11959); Pythia-160m ranks it first after the all-English context (p ~ 0.80).
author: LS-NEQ stimulus authoring (F11A, teacher Mia / chemistry lesson)
notes: Formulation A. Ten meaning units: Mia teaches a chemistry lesson / the students sit at long tables / Mia pours a liquid into a beaker / the liquid turns red / a boy asks about the colour / Mia writes a formula on the board / a burner heats the water / steam rises from the flask / the students note the result / the lesson ends with the bell. Subjects alternate between the protagonist (Mia), other people (the students, a boy) and objects or substances (the liquid, a burner, steam, the lesson), singular and plural, so C3 switches cross real subject-verb agreement; units 2, 8 and 10 have bare intransitive predicates (sit/sitzen, rises/steigt, ends/endet) and unit 4 a copular predicate (turns red/wird rot). No separable German verbs ('aufsteigen', 'anschreiben' avoided). 'Mia' is the only proper name. Present tense and positive polarity throughout; unit 9 reads naturally in German, units 1 and 10 in English.
